attempts.label: CRCNS:ac-2
attempts.entry_title: Shared and private variability in the auditory cortex (DeWeese and Zador 2004)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held in this data: the split of variability into a shared part and a small private part (best private estimate near 1.5 mV), the total variability across neurons, the drop after LFP-based culling, and the negative link between spontaneous activity and the evoked response. The random-culling controls did not reproduce (3.82 mV against 4.5), most likely because the paper's handling of its 10-trial rule is unclear. PSP-based culling alone and the largest LFP-based reduction held only in part. The miniature EPSP size could not be pinned down, since the paper gives no detection method. Many outcomes depend on a spike-removal rule the paper does not describe, which the agent assumed.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of DeWeese and Zador (2004) on CRCNS data set ac-2, which holds the paper's 33 in vivo whole-cell recordings from rat auditory cortex during pure tones, 29 of them with a simultaneous LFP, and six recordings after TTX. It measures the variability index of tone-evoked PSPs, partitions it into private and shared parts with the paper's LFP- and PSP-based culling and estimation procedures, and checks the controls, the large-response and CV analyses, the spontaneous veto, the anesthesia groups and the recording properties.

notebooks.title: Reproducing DeWeese and Zador (2004) from CRCNS ac-2

outcomes.notes: In 022801md01b (20 trials per tone) the 32 mean responses peak 26.5 to 41.5 ms after onset with heights 1.19 to 18.12 mV, within the widened ranges, under both peak windows. Normalized and aligned on their peaks they correlate with their average with median r 0.991 (minimum 0.933), above 0.9. The mean response to each neuron's largest tone peaks within 50 ms of onset in 19 of 33 neurons with the peak searched after onset (20.75 to 115.5 ms, median 45.25) or in the culling window (20.75 to 84.75 ms), so the all-neurons part fails under the claims file's 50 ms bound. The responses begin 14.25 to 38.5 ms after onset in 32 neurons (the mean over all tones first above 1 mV; 021401md02 never exceeds it).
deviations: Trials are each neuron's stable epoch, cycles first_cycle to last_cycle of the data set's cell_specific_parameters.m; the paper requires 10 consecutive stable repetitions, and these epochs give its repetition counts (mean 18.1, 10 to 63).
The alignment window is 100 ms placed around each peak as the culling window sits around the median latency, with edge values where it runs off the trace (a plotting choice).

PSP-based culling removes 24.1% of trials (pooled; 19.2% mean of neurons), outside 29 +- 2.9, and LFP-based culling 37.8%. Without the tone criteria applied again after random culling, the LFP-matched control gives 4.83 mV (SD over simulations 0.97) and the PSP-matched one is unstable (2.30 mV, SD 8.5). Whether the paper applied them again is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-ac-2.yaml). The claims file's spike rule gives 4.36, 3.74 and 3.98 mV; the outcome is the same. outcomes.notes: Total CV 0.371 +- 0.027 (19 neurons, at least 15 mV) and 0.734 +- 0.042 (33, all tones), matching 0.37 and 0.73. Private CV 0.265 +- 0.021 (14), within 0.27 +- 0.01, and 0.383 +- 0.026 (28), 0.007 below 0.41 +- 0.02. The large responses' private CV is significantly lower by Student's t-test (p = 0.0055) and the paired test (p < 0.0001). The criterion's reproduced outcome needs all four values, so the claim holds in part; the criterion defines no outcome for a value outside tolerance with the test holding, and partially reproduced is used. The peak-to-trough height over the trace (2b) gives 0.268 and 0.402, all four holding; the claims file's spike rule gives a large-response total CV of 0.491 and no significant difference (p = 0.475). Spikethresh keeping the slow events gives a total CV of 0.468 and no significant difference (p = 0.136); the -20 mV rule at any rise gives private CVs of 0.286 and 0.389 (p = 0.014), and heights re-measured after culling 0.267 and 0.385, partially reproduced.

outcomes.notes: The six TTX recordings are digitized in steps of 0.049 mV (0.012 for 030401md02h after its gain of 4), with 14% to 68% of the differences between samples 0. Template matching at thresholds of 3 to 5 finds up to 29 events per s and, on the inverted traces, 55% to 80% as many (mean over recordings), so most of its events are noise; its mean scale is 0.28 to 0.35 mV. The derivative detector with, per recording, the lowest threshold at which the inverted trace gives at most 10% as many events (k = 3 to 6) gives a mean size of 0.602 +- 0.164 mV over five recordings, outside 0.39 +- 0.08, and a mean CV of 0.354, within 0.36 +- 0.03. 050401md02 has one stable sweep (7.7 s) and no threshold meets the bound. The event-triggered averages rise within about 2 ms and peak at 0.15 to 0.99 mV; 6.7% to 12.0% of events fall in the 50 ms after a tone, against 10% by chance. The result moves with the choices: fixed thresholds k = 3 and 4 give 0.370 mV (CV 0.421) and 0.487 mV (CV 0.350), each with one value holding; bounds of 5% and 20% give 0.702 and 0.549 mV (CV 0.314 and 0.376); the documentation's file order gives 0.726 mV (CV 0.296). No reading with the false positives bounded gives both values. Question for the paper's authors: how were mEPSPs detected and sized (detector, threshold, filtering, baseline), and which sweeps of each TTX recording were used? Under the main reading event rates range from 0.11 Hz (030401md02h, 15 events, 1.04 mV) to 19 Hz (050801md01c, 0.20 mV, sizes down to 0.01 mV), so the mean rests on the threshold each recording gets. Without 030401md02h the four others give 0.492 mV and CV 0.385, both outside.
deviations: Sweeps are first_trial to last_trial of each TTX recording's cell_specific_parameters.m, read as ep_<trial - 1>, without their first 0.3 s; the documentation's name order (dir) and all sweeps are shown. 030401md02h is divided by its documented gain of 4.

The detector is assumed: a threshold on the derivative of the trace smoothed over 1 ms, in noise SDs (SD after clipping at 3 SD), set per recording as the lowest of k = 3 to 8 at which the sign-inverted trace gives at most 10% as many events; size is the peak in the 10 ms after onset minus the mean of the 2 ms before. Template matching (Clements and Bekkers 1997) is shown; on the inverted traces it finds most of the events it finds on the traces.

outcomes.notes: Repetitions 18.12 +- 1.93 (SE), 10 to 63. Rest potential from the 15-ms baselines corrected by -12 mV, median -70.0, range -58.4 to -92.0 mV; from the sweeps outside the prepulse, -68.6 and -55.3 to -87.9. Input resistance from the prepulse is 58.2 to 438.3 MOhm (median 137.9) as measured, outside the range; minus the recorded access resistance it is 19.1 to 140.6 MOhm (median 65.1), as in the paper (19 to 141, median 64).
deviations: Input resistance is the steady-state prepulse response (last 20% of the step, against the 5 ms before it) divided by the step current, minus the recorded access resistance. The Methods say there was no on-line series resistance compensation, so the step response includes the access resistance; the paper does not say it was subtracted. This is an assumption; without it the claim is not reproduced.
The prepulse height is read as a current in pA, as the docs table says for 110900md05, not the mV the documentation states.
Rest potential corrected by -12 mV (the paper), with the documentation's 10 mV shown.

Access resistance, Pearson r = 0.087 (p = 0.631), Spearman 0.155 (p = 0.390); depth over 25 neurons with a recorded depth, r = -0.273 (p = 0.187), rho = -0.338 (p = 0.098). With the claims file's spike rule the groups are 5.70 and 4.99 mV, the first outside, and no correlation is significant (p = 0.125 to 0.661). The -20 mV rule at any rise gives 4.50 and 4.36 mV with no significant correlation; spikethresh keeping the slow events gives 5.22 mV for the upper group, outside.

findings.statement: Anesthetized_cell_info.txt gives a junction potential of about 10 mV and says the true potentials are about 10 mV more depolarized than the recorded values. The paper corrects by 12 mV in the other direction (more hyperpolarized), and only that correction gives the paper's rest potentials (median -70.0 mV, -58.4 to -92.0) from the recorded baselines; the documented direction gives -33 to -66 mV.

Each anesthetized neuron's cell_specific_parameters.m gives first_cycle, last_cycle, spikethresh and sweeps_to_include_in_bumps_anl, which the documentation does not describe for these neurons. The cycles give the paper's stable epochs (repetitions 10 to 63, mean 18.1) and spikethresh its spike removal (with them the paper's population values follow), so they carry the paper's trial selection.

The documentation calls the prepulse height a voltage ("height (negative mV)"); the values (100 and 200) are currents in pA, as the cell table's note for 110900md05 (-200 pA to -100 pA) and the input resistances they give show.
Sutter_diag_depth is missing (empty or NaN) for 8 of the 33 anesthetized neurons, so the paper's depth range and its depth comparison can be checked on 25.

The TTX recording 030401md02h, after the documented division by 4, sits near +2.6 mV (1st to 99th percentile -5.0 to 6.1 mV), which is not a membrane potential; the other TTX recordings sit at -54 to -71 mV. Its offset or gain may be wrong.

The paper does not say how spike trials were found. The claims file's rule (a fast rise to above -20 mV after the junction potential correction, with 10 mV/ms for the rise) and the data set's per-neuron spikethresh give different results (mean total variability 5.35 against 4.58 mV); without the rise criterion the -20 mV rule gives 4.43 mV. Spikethresh also removes slow depolarizations to about -10 mV, which may be regenerative events or large PSPs; keeping them gives 5.11 mV. Spikethresh was assumed. Question for the authors, were spikes removed with spikethresh, as a height above the 15-ms baseline, and were the slow depolarizations removed as spikes?

The paper does not say whether input resistance had the access resistance subtracted; only with it subtracted do the prepulse responses give the paper's 19 to 141 MOhm (median 64). Question for the authors: was input resistance the step response minus the access resistance, and over which part of the step?

The paper gives no method for detecting and sizing mEPSPs. With fixed thresholds of 3 to 5 noise SDs the mean size is 0.28 to 0.43 mV for template matching (CV 0.37 to 0.60) and 0.37 to 0.63 mV for the derivative detector (CV 0.33 to 0.53); with the derivative detector and a false-positive bound of 5% to 20% it is 0.55 to 0.77 mV (CV 0.27 to 0.40), over the two sweep mappings of the stable epochs. Question for the authors, which detector, threshold, filter and baseline were used, and which sweeps?

Several details of the variability procedures are not given and move counts near their tolerances: the window searched for the mean PSP's peak, the span of the culling threshold's peak-to-trough height, whether the negative scale factor rule applies to PSP-based culling, whether the tone criteria use the mean before or after culling, whether heights are re-measured after culling, and whether the random culling controls apply the 10-trial criterion again. Question for the authors: how was each set?

Each TTX recording's cell_specific_parameters.m gives first_trial and last_trial, but the documentation does not say which ep_<n>.ibw file is trial k. Its Matlab example lists the files with dir('ep_*.ibw'), which orders them by name (ep_0, ep_1, ep_10, ...), and that order picks different sweeps from the numeric one in four of the six recordings (050301md01, 050501md01, 050501md04, 050801md01c). 050401md02 has one stable sweep of 7.7 s.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive listing against the notebook's MD5 sums and tested the helper functions on synthetic inputs. 22 of its 23 outcomes agree with the record; for mepsp-size it gives partially reproduced where the record blocked the claim. Its general points: the main reading mixes readings across claims (psp-culling passes under 1b or 3, fig4c under the -20 mV rule, fig8 under (a,b)), and the -20 mV variant was not the claims file's rule.

disagreements.reason: Labelled blocked although the archive holds all six TTX recordings and the documented gain, and the claims file's detector readings were run, so it is testable. The derivative detector at k = 3-4 gives 0.34-0.41 mV, within 0.39 +- 0.08; the CV is out under all six readings and the template detector gives 0.17 mV. For 050801md01c the derivative detector barely responds to its threshold, which suggests the robust noise SD has collapsed and the detector picks up noise; the template detector finds 15-28 Hz of 0.1-0.2-mV events; amplitude on the smoothed trace inflates noise events; the mapping of sweep files is not checked, and 050401md02 uses a single 7.7-s sweep.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook with the conclusions and the summary, the helper module, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 23 outcomes. It found statements the numbers do not support (cells 14, 29, 44, the lfp-culling notes and the mEPSP finding) and readings the record did not name. Remaining points, the mEPSP mean rests on per-recording thresholds; heights are not re-measured after culling and this was not run as a reading; the claims file's rule depends on the 10 mV/ms rise chosen here and the slow depolarizations that only spikethresh removes could be large PSPs; the culling-controls question is unanswered; the fig2, fig3a and fig4 panels had not been compared with the paper by eye.

entries.name: crcns-ac-2-deweese-2004
entries.title: Shared and private variability in the auditory cortex (DeWeese and Zador 2004)
entries.description: Tests the findings of DeWeese and Zador (2004) on CRCNS data set ac-2, which holds the paper's 33 in vivo whole-cell recordings from rat auditory cortex during pure tones, 29 of them with a simultaneous LFP, and six recordings after TTX. It measures the variability index of tone-evoked PSPs, partitions it into private and shared parts with the paper's LFP- and PSP-based culling and estimation procedures, and checks the controls, the large-response and CV analyses, the spontaneous veto, the anesthesia groups and the recording properties.

notebooks.title: Reproducing DeWeese and Zador (2004) from CRCNS ac-2
